facts.setting: on appeal, a request for a hearing submitted to the Office of Administrative Courts
facts.value: No later than sixty (60) calendar days after the date of the Notice of Action.
facts.counts_from: the date of the Notice of Action
facts.note: Colorado's own choice of the reasonable time that 42 CFR 431.221(d) caps at 90 days from the date the notice of action is mailed, so not a conflict in the number. The counting event differs: the rule counts from the date of the Notice of Action and HCPF's page from the date in it, and neither says whether that is the mailing date; that is an open question. HCPF's page also says "You generally have 60 days" (docs/domain/sources/colorado/hcpf-appeals-2026-10-17.html:1006), a hedge the rule does not make. 8.057.3.F.1 at line 2765 of the extraction has similar words about the informal dispute resolution conference and is not this paragraph. 8.057.4.B.1 was read on rendered page 78. The PDF prints no date of its own, so its source_date is not stated; it is version 12612 of 10 CCR 2505-10 8.000, which the Secretary of State's rule-information page shows as the current version with effective date 07/10/2026 and filing type Emergency Rule (docs/domain/sources/colorado/10-ccr-2505-10-8.000-rule-information-2026-10-17.html:241 and :248), read 2026-10-17. How long the emergency rule lasts, and whether the permanent rule changes 8.057, was not read: recheck on state rule, when 8.000 is next filed or the emergency rule lapses. Whether a person asked in time is the agency's determination.

facts.setting: on appeal, after the date of action, for a member
facts.value: Where the member requests a hearing not more than ten (10) days after the date of action, the member’s services must be reinstated back to the date of action and continued until a final agency decision is rendered after the hearing, unless it is determined at the hearing that the sole issue is one of federal or state law or policy.
facts.note: Colorado's own choice: 42 CFR 431.231(a) says the agency "may" reinstate, and 8.057.5.D says "must", and adds that services are reinstated back to the date of action, which 431.231(a) does not say. The two sources disagree, and that is an open question for HCPF or the Office of Administrative Courts: the rule has the member request a hearing "not more than ten (10) days after" the date of action, while HCPF's page, under its heading "Eligibility appeals" (docs/domain/sources/colorado/hcpf-appeals-2026-10-17.html:1140), says the Office of Administrative Courts must "get your request for an appeal" no later than 10 days "after the date of action" (:1148). A request sent in time by the rule's words could arrive late by the page's. Under that heading the page says a current Health First Colorado member (:1143) whose request arrives in time keeps coverage: "Your coverage will continue until a final decision is made on your appeal." (:1150). It also says a person applying for the first time who does not qualify can appeal, but "there is no continuation of benefits" (:1151). An appeal of a disenrollment for noncompliance is read here as an eligibility appeal; the page does not name community engagement. The page's separate "Benefits appeals" section (:1152) is the services case: if HCPF stopped or reduced "a service we previously authorized" (:1153), the Office of Administrative Courts "must receive your request for an appeal" no later than 10 days from the date of action (:1154). 8.057.5.D was read on rendered page 81. The rule's dates and emergency status are as in the hearing-request-window fact: version 12612, Emergency Rule, effective 07/10/2026; recheck on state rule when 8.000 is next filed or the emergency rule lapses. Whether a request came within the 10 days is the agency's determination.

facts.setting: on appeal, before the date of action, for a member
facts.value: Where the member requests a hearing before the date of action, the member’s benefits or services may not be terminated or reduced until a final agency decision is rendered after the hearing unless: 1. It is determined at the hearing that the sole issue is one of federal or state law or policy; and 2. If it is determined at the hearing that the sole issue is one of federal or state law in accordance with section 8.057.5.A.1., the member must be promptly informed in writing that services are to be terminated or reduced pending the hearing decision.
facts.note: Not a period, so no counts_from. 8.057.5.A does not make the protection depend on the agency having sent the 10-day or 5-day notice under 42 CFR 431.211 or 431.214, as 431.230(a) does; that it otherwise matches 431.230(a) is a reading of both, not a statement in either. 8.057.5.A was read on rendered page 81. The rule's dates and emergency status are as in the hearing-request-window fact: version 12612, Emergency Rule, effective 07/10/2026; recheck on state rule when 8.000 is next filed or the emergency rule lapses. Whether a request came before the date of action is the agency's determination, and whether the sole issue is one of law or policy is determined at the hearing.

facts.setting: at renewal (redetermination), under a draft rule that is not adopted
facts.value: If available and reliable information is insufficient to establish a Specified Exclusion, Mandatory Exception, or compliance through a Qualifying Activity, a Work Requirements Self-Reporting Form and any required verification requests shall be provided with the redetermination form. The individual shall be provided at least 30 calendar days to provide information establishing that Community Engagement requirements have been met; or The requirement does not apply. The due date for the Work Requirement Self-Reporting Form will align with the redetermination due date.
facts.note: Inferred, and the draft is not adopted. The draft names neither 42 CFR 435.558(b)(2) option. That Colorado's draft takes renewal-notice-with-renewal-form is inferred from three things read in it: the form is a notice of noncompliance, since the draft's unlabeled paragraph on page 23 (margin lines 885 to 890, extraction lines 1843 to 1846) issues a Work Requirements Form as a notice of noncompliance, and at application h.ii.4 names "A Work Requirements Self-Reporting Form (Notice of Noncompliance)" (extraction line 1860); at renewal it goes with the redetermination form (h.iii.2); and its due date is the redetermination due date (h.iii.3). The next two paragraphs may add a second, shorter period: if the individual returns the redetermination form but the information is incomplete, inconsistent, or raises additional questions, the eligibility site worker will make reasonable efforts to obtain clarification (h.iii.4, margin lines 941 to 944, extraction line 1936), and the individual will be provided at least 10 business days to submit additional requested verification (h.iii.5, margin lines 945 and 946, extraction line 1940). The draft does not say whether those 10 business days cover community engagement information or how they sit with the 30 calendar days, so whether a person has one window or two under the draft is not known. Research L5-3 makes the same mapping and calls it inference. Paragraph labels h.iii.2 to h.iii.5 were read on rendered page 24, h.iii.2 and h.iii.3 on 2026-10-17 and h.iii.4 and h.iii.5 on 2026-10-18, since the extraction separates them from their text. The draft does not say what the 30 days count from at renewal, where 435.558(a)(2) counts from receipt; at application it gives 30 calendar days from receipt (page 23, margin lines 915 to 919). So counts_from is not published. On 2026-10-23 the 8.000 and draft 8.100 extractions, the 8.000 rule-information page and HCPF's appeals page, which with the two PDFs the extractions come from are the six stored Colorado files, were searched, ignoring case, for 30 calendar days, 30-calendar, 30- calendar, from receipt, considered received, due date, redetermination form and self-reporting form. The only hits that name what a period counts from are the draft's application paragraph, "30- calendar days from receipt" and the 5 days after which the notice counts as received (extraction lines 1870 and 1872); its renewal paragraph's hits (lines 1929 to 1942) name no event, and the 8.000 extraction's hits are on provider appeals, exceptions to an initial decision and a provider's records (lines 2580, 3069 to 3087 and 4194). (Corrected 2026-10-23: said "That is an open question for HCPF.", and counts_from said "not stated; the draft says only that the form's due date will align with the redetermination due date"; decision record 0006.) This fact takes Colorado's part of two open questions, both raised 2026-10-17: "Which renewal option applies where a state's plan records no choice?", for the choice, and "What do the at least 30 days in Colorado's draft renewal paragraph count from, and could they give fewer than 30 days from receipt, or more than the 30 days the preamble says cannot be extended?", for counts_from. (Added 2026-10-23; decision record 0006.) The PDF prints no date; its file name carries 2026-09-28, the HCPF stakeholder meeting it was posted for (manifest note). Research ledger L5-1 reports, from an HCPF deck that is not stored, a Medical Services Board reading on 2026-11-27 and effect on 2027-01-01: recheck on state rule when 8.100 is adopted. Shown as known, this fact would be dangerous. Whether a person's information establishes compliance is the agency's determination.

facts.setting: between renewals, in a state that verifies compliance more often than at renewal under 42 CFR 435.557(d)
facts.note: No stored Colorado source says whether Colorado verifies compliance more often than at renewal under 42 CFR 435.557(d), or, if it does, which of the two choices of 42 CFR 435.558(b)(3) it takes: sending the notice of noncompliance straight after its data check, more-frequent-check-notice-after-data-check, or asking for information first, more-frequent-check-notice-after-information-request. On 2026-10-23 the 8.000 and draft 8.100 extractions, the 8.000 rule-information page and HCPF's appeals page, which with the two PDFs the extractions come from are the six stored Colorado files, were searched, ignoring case, for more frequent, more often, between renewal, between redetermination, periodic, quarterly, monthly, each month, every month, ex parte, 435.557, 435.558, data match, interim, post-enrollment, post enrollment, ongoing, throughout, frequen and verif. No hit says that Colorado verifies more often than at renewal or names either choice. The nearest are in the draft 8.100, which is not adopted and so chooses nothing. For a member who remains an applicable individual and reports a change to a qualifying activity, it says "Community Engagement compliance shall be evaluated at the member's next scheduled renewal using the lookback review period, unless another change affects the member's eligibility or establishes that the member is a Specified Excluded Individual." (extraction lines 1394 to 1397). For a member who loses a specified exclusion between renewals, the Department determines compliance over a lookback review period that ends on the last day of the month before the month the member becomes an applicable individual (lines 1361 to 1366). The draft does not say whether that determination is a verification more often than at renewal in the sense of 42 CFR 435.557(d), and reading it either way is inference. Those lines follow 42 CFR 435.556(a)(2)(iii) closely, the review period for a person who becomes an applicable individual as a result of a redetermination based on a change in circumstances (docs/domain/cms-2454-ifc/2026-11094.xml:3800, 91 FR 33474), which the rule keeps apart from § 435.556(a)(2)(ii), the period for a State that has opted to conduct more frequent verifications under § 435.557(d) (:3799). And the draft's part h, Compliance Reporting and Verification (extraction line 1766), has a part for verification at application (line 1847) and one for redetermination (line 1918), and none for checks between renewals. Both lean toward the draft making no check between renewals, which is inference, and the draft does not say it makes neither choice and is not adopted, so the fact stays not published. The draft's ex parte hits are about redetermination (lines 302, 306, 1445 and 1919), and its 435.557 hit is the verification period at application (line 1859); the 8.000 extraction's monthly and data match hits are on premiums, payments and data from other parties (lines 3425 to 3598). This fact takes Colorado's part of the open question "Which option applies to checks between renewals where a state's plan records no choice?", raised 2026-10-17. Recheck on state rule, when 8.100 is adopted. Whether a person met the requirement is the agency's determination.

facts.setting: at renewal, for people already enrolled in a 12-month eligibility period in the adult expansion group on January 1, 2027, whose renewals are already scheduled in 2027
facts.note: No stored Colorado source says which of CMS SMD 26-001's two transition paths Colorado took: moving renewals already scheduled in 2027 earlier, reschedule-2027-renewals-to-six-months, or keeping them where they are, keep-scheduled-2027-renewals. On 2026-10-23 the 8.000 and draft 8.100 extractions, the 8.000 rule-information page and HCPF's appeals page, which with the two PDFs the extractions come from are the six stored Colorado files, were searched, ignoring case, for 26-001, reschedul, six-month, 6-month, six month, 6 month, transition, initiation, 2027, renewal date, 12-month, 12 month, twelve and eligibility period. No hit names a path. The two 26-001 hits are eDocket numbers on the rule-information page, 2026-00141 and 2026-00116, that contain 26-001 by chance (lines 346 and 394). The draft 8.100's one 2027 hit is the start of the community engagement requirement, "Effective January 1, 2027" (extraction line 1117). The other hits are on other subjects, among them a disability expected to last six months or longer (line 62), Transitional Medical Assistance (line 722), a member who transitions into the MAGI Expansion Group from another group (line 1371), presumptive eligibility once every 12 months (line 1035) and, in the 8.000 extraction, 6 months after a Medicare claim's disposition (line 2290); the appeals page's two transition hits are in its style sheet. The search of 2026-10-17, for the first four of these words over the same four files, found the same two eDocket numbers and nothing else. This fact takes the open question "Which SMD 26-001 transition path did Colorado take for renewals already scheduled in 2027?", raised 2026-10-17, which moved here whole. Recheck on state plan amendment or CMS guidance. Whether a person is in the adult expansion group, and when their renewal is, is the agency's determination.
